bottom_line: The ratings mostly hold: futures are flat to slightly up after the market absorbed Huang's resignation, and the power, grid and cooling names sit in segments the worldview still rates overweight. But October PPI lands before the open with the 10-year at 5.1%, and Nvidia reports on Tuesday, so start small rather than full.
what_changed: S&P 500 futures about +0.2% and Nasdaq 100 roughly flat before October PPI (expected +0.4%); 10-year near 5.10%. Touches the 'crowded at high rates' thesis.
Nvidia named CFO Colette Kress interim CEO and confirmed Q3 results on Tue 17 Nov after the close; shares recovered slightly after hours. A near-term catalyst for every AI supplier.
Cisco beat with revenue +24% and a bigger AI forecast but was flat after hours on margin pressure from component shortages; Cerebras rose about 16% on a Microsoft deal.
Applied Materials reported after Thursday's close (the digest shows a Q4 beat); its 380.95 rating price predates the market's reaction.

names.take: Segment overweight and only +3% since rated; a Samsung–Modine bid would support cooling multiples. Fine for a small start.

trust: No ratings are graded yet (grading starts after 28 days). So far picks rated Buy/Overweight are +1.1% vs QQQ, ahead of the screen's no-AI #1 (-1.5%) and a random shortlist pick (-0.1%), but the sample is small and young.
if_buying: Overweight means a small starter position, not full size.
Prefer names near their rated price in overweight segments (VRT, VST, AAON, ETN); skip ANET and PWR at these levels.
Wait on AMAT until it has traded after its results, and on DELL until Nvidia reports on 17 Nov.
Use limit orders: PPI at 21:30 SGT can swing the open.
